**Conclusion:**  
Local tool-calling language models offer enhanced functionality, cost-efficiency, and control but face limitations in technical implementation, framework dependencies, and consistency. Key findings balance benefits like automation capabilities against challenges such as imperfect estimators and operational bugs.

**Key Findings:**  
1. **Benefits:**  
   - **Enhanced Automation:** Tool calling bridges LLMs and external APIs, enabling action-oriented AI systems (Adaline.ai).  
   - **Cost-Efficiency & Control:** Local LLMs provide privacy and reduced cloud dependency, though structured tool use varies by model (Docker blog).  
   - **Performance Leadership:** Qwen models excel in local tool-calling benchmarks, outperforming others (Docker blog).  

2. **Limitations:**  
   - **Technical Challenges:** Frameworks like ArXiv’s approach face issues with imperfect estimators and suboptimal cost-aware decisions (arXiv).  
   - **Implementation Dependencies:** Limited tool-calling support in local setups without external agent frameworks (Hugging Face forum).  
   - **Operational Bugs:** Issues like inconsistent triggers, infinite loops, and prompt inefficiencies hinder reliability (Dev.to).  

**Source URLs:**  
- [Adaline.ai: LLM Tool Calling](https://www.adaline.ai/blog/understanding-llms-and-tool-calling)  
- [ArXiv: Tool Calling Framework](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.00737v1)  
- [Docker Blog: Local LLM Tool Calling](https://www.docker.com/blog/local-llm-tool-calling-a-practical-evaluation)  
- [Hugging Face Forum](https://discuss.huggingface.co/t/tool-function-calling-abilities-of-llms-that-are-used-locally-pulled-through-ollama/165277)  
- [Dev.to: Local LLM Tool Calling Limitations](https://dev.to/docteurrs/calling-code-with-local-llm-is-a-hoax-2n51)  

**Note:** Some claims rely on technical papers and community discussions, with limitations tied to specific frameworks or models.
